blocks.text: The **Delhi Sultanate (1206–1526)** was **Islamic rule's first enduring north-Indian state**, spanning **five dynasties — Slave/Mamluk, Khilji, Tughlaq, Sayyid and Lodi** — from **Qutbuddin Aibak** to **Ibrahim Lodi**, ended by **Babur at Panipat (1526)**.

rows: **Qutbuddin Aibak** (founder; Qutb Minar begun), **Iltutmish** (real consolidator; iqta; Qutb Minar completed), **Razia** (first woman ruler), **Balban** (kingship theory 'zill-i-ilahi').
**Alauddin Khilji** — market/price control, revenue reforms, repelled Mongols; **Malik Kafur's Deccan raids**.
**Muhammad bin Tughlaq** (capital to Daulatabad, token currency — failed), **Firoz Shah** (canals, jizya).

sections.heading: 🔎 Exam-ready deep coverage: the five Sultanate dynasties

rows: **Qutbuddin Aibak** (founder; Quwwat-ul-Islam, Qutb Minar begun; d. polo fall); **Iltutmish** (real consolidator; Iqta system; silver **tanka** & copper **jital**; Chihalgani/'Forty'); **Razia Sultana** (only woman ruler of Delhi); **Balban** (blood-and-iron; Sijda & Paibos; Persian court).

**Jalaluddin**; **Alauddin Khilji** — **market/price control (Diwan-i-Riyasat)**, first standing army with **dagh (branding) & chehra (descriptive roll)**, land measurement (biswa), 50% land tax; **Malik Kafur's Deccan raids**; Alai Darwaza & Siri fort.

**Ghiyasuddin**; **Muhammad-bin-Tughlaq** — capital transfer **Delhi↔Daulatabad**, token **copper/bronze currency** (failed), Khorasan/Qarachil schemes; **Firoz Shah Tughlaq** — irrigation canals, Jizya on Brahmins, Diwan-i-Khairat, brought Ashokan pillars to Delhi.
Bahlul Lodi; **Sikandar Lodi** (founded **Agra**, 1504); **Ibrahim Lodi** — defeated & killed by **Babur at Panipat I (1526)**.

blocks.text: Alauddin Khilji's **market reforms** and Muhammad-bin-Tughlaq's **two failed experiments (capital shift + token currency)** are the most-asked Sultanate facts.

items: Memorise the 5-dynasty order and one signature ruler/fact each — the exam's staple.
Aibak founder; Iltutmish consolidator; Panipat 1526 = end of Sultanate / start of Mughals.

prelimsPointers: Five dynasties — **Slave/Mamluk → Khilji → Tughlaq → Sayyid → Lodi**.
**Qutbuddin Aibak** — founder; began the **Qutb Minar**; **Iltutmish** completed it & introduced **iqta** and the silver **tanka** & copper **jital**.
**Razia Sultan** — first (and only) woman ruler of the Sultanate.
**Balban** — theory of kingship: king as **'zill-i-ilahi' (shadow of God)**; sijda & paibos.
**Sayyids** founded by **Khizr Khan** (Timur's deputy); **Lodis** — first Afghan dynasty (Bahlul Lodi).
**Sikandar Lodi** founded **Agra**; **Ibrahim Lodi** defeated by **Babur at Panipat (1526)**.
The Sultanate was an **Islamic theocratic-military state** ruled by the Sultan aided by the **wazir**.
Five dynasties: **Slave → Khilji → Tughlaq → Sayyid → Lodi** (1206–1526).
**Iltutmish** — silver **tanka** & copper **jital**; completed **Qutb Minar**; **Razia** = only woman Sultan.
**Alauddin Khilji** — market control, **dagh & chehra**, Malik Kafur's south raids.
**Muhammad-bin-Tughlaq** — Delhi↔**Daulatabad** shift & **token currency** (both failed).
**Ibrahim Lodi** killed at **Panipat I (1526)** by **Babur**; **Sikandar Lodi** founded **Agra**.
mainsAngles: Trace the political evolution of the Delhi Sultanate across its five dynasties.

glossary.definition: The 'Slave' dynasty of Turkish military slaves who founded the Delhi Sultanate.
A revenue assignment granted for military/administrative service, systematised by Iltutmish.
'Shadow of God' — Balban's exalted theory of divine kingship.

blocks.text: The Delhi Sultanate ran a **centralised, Persianised military-theocratic administration** built on the **iqta system**, funded by **land revenue and market controls**, and produced a new **Indo-Islamic urban society** — most vividly reformed by **Alauddin Khilji** and experimented with by **Muhammad bin Tughlaq**.

rows: Revenue assignment for service; **iqtadars/muqtis** collected revenue & maintained troops.
**Market/price control**, revenue at 50% (measurement), standing army, branding of horses (dagh) & muster roll (chehra).
Urban growth (Delhi a world city — **Ibn Battuta**), new crafts (paper, spinning wheel), Persian bureaucracy, slave labour (Firoz).

sections.heading: 🔎 Exam-ready deep coverage: Sultanate administration, economy, society

items: **Theory of kingship**: Sultan as head; based on Islamic law (Shariat) tempered by Zawabit (state law); **Ulema** influence; **Balban** raised royal prestige (Zill-i-Ilahi).

**Central departments**: **Diwan-i-Wizarat** (finance — Wazir), **Diwan-i-Arz** (military — Ariz-i-Mumalik), **Diwan-i-Insha** (correspondence), **Diwan-i-Risalat** (religious/appeals); **Barid** (intelligence).
**Iqta system**: land-revenue assignments to nobles (**Iqtadars/Muqtis**) in lieu of salary & for maintaining troops — the fiscal backbone (systematised by **Iltutmish**).
**Revenue**: land tax (**Kharaj**, up to 50% under Alauddin), **Jizya** (non-Muslims), **Zakat, Khams** (1/5 war booty); measurement/**hasil**.

**Economy & society**: **urbanisation, market economy, new crafts** (paper, textiles), the **Persian wheel (rahat)** & **spinning wheel (charkha)** spread; Sufi khanqahs; slavery (Firoz's 1.8 lakh slaves); a composite **Indo-Islamic (Ganga-Jamuni)** culture emerged.
Iqta = fiscal-military backbone; Alauddin's market control & army reforms; MBT's two failed experiments.
Ibn Battuta (Moroccan) visited under Muhammad bin Tughlaq — key traveller.

prelimsPointers: Key ministries — **Diwan-i-Wizarat (revenue), Diwan-i-Arz (military, under Ariz-i-mumalik), Diwan-i-Insha, Diwan-i-Risalat**.
**Iqta system** — revenue assignment for military service (iqtadar/muqti).
**Alauddin Khilji** — **market/price control**, land revenue at ~50%, **dagh (horse branding) & chehra (soldier descriptive roll)**.
**Muhammad bin Tughlaq** — capital shift to **Daulatabad** & **token (copper) currency**; both failed.
**Firoz Shah Tughlaq** — dug canals, built towns (Firozabad, Hisar), imposed **jizya** on Brahmins, employed slaves (Diwan-i-Bandagan).
**Ibn Battuta** (Morocco) visited under MBT; wrote **Rihla**.
New technologies — **paper, spinning wheel (charkha), Persian wheel** entered India.
Departments: **Diwan-i-Wizarat (finance), Diwan-i-Arz (army), Diwan-i-Insha, Diwan-i-Risalat**.
**Iqta** = revenue-assignment to nobles (systematised by **Iltutmish**); holder = **Muqti/Iqtadar**.
Taxes: **Kharaj** (land), **Jizya** (non-Muslims), **Zakat, Khams**; Alauddin's land tax ~**50%**.
New tech spread: **Persian wheel, spinning wheel (charkha), paper**; composite Indo-Islamic culture.
mainsAngles: Examine Alauddin Khilji's administrative and market reforms.

glossary.definition: The holder of an iqta, responsible for revenue collection and maintaining troops.
Alauddin's system of branding horses (dagh) and keeping soldiers' descriptive rolls (chehra) to prevent fraud.
Muhammad bin Tughlaq's ill-fated copper/brass coinage meant to circulate at silver value.

blocks.text: The Sultanate created the **Indo-Islamic architectural style** — the **arch, dome and minaret** married to Indian craft — from the **Qutb complex to Tughlaq forts** — and a flourishing **Persian literature (Amir Khusrau)** that seeded **Urdu, qawwali and Hindustani music**.

rows: **Qutb Minar, Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque** (Aibak/Iltutmish); **arcuate** (true arch) style begins.
**Alai Darwaza** (first true dome/arch), Siri fort — Seljuk influence.
Austere, sloping-wall forts — **Tughlaqabad, Firozabad, Kotla**; batter walls.
**Lodi Gardens** tombs; the octagonal & double-dome tomb form.
**Amir Khusrau** ('Tuti-i-Hind'/parrot of India) — Persian poetry, credited with **qawwali, sitar/tabla, Khari Boli** roots; **Ziauddin Barani** (Tarikh-i-Firozshahi).

sections.heading: 🔎 Exam-ready deep coverage: Sultanate art, architecture & letters

items: **Architecture — the arcuate style** (true **arch & dome**, lime mortar) replacing trabeate; materials — red sandstone, later marble; motifs — geometric, arabesque, calligraphy (no figures).

**Monuments**: **Qutb Minar** (Aibak-Iltutmish), **Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque** (first, from temple spolia), **Alai Darwaza** (Alauddin — first true dome), **Siri** fort, **Tughlaqabad** & sloping-wall Tughlaq style, **Firoz Shah Kotla**, **Lodi tombs** (double-dome).

**Literature**: **Amir Khusrau** ('Tuti-i-Hind', father of **Qawwali** & Khari Boli/Urdu, invented the **sitar/tabla** by tradition; works — Tughlaq Nama, Khazain-ul-Futuh); **Ziauddin Barani** (Tarikh-i-Firozshahi), **Minhaj-us-Siraj** (Tabaqat-i-Nasiri), **Ibn Battuta** (Rihla — visited Muhammad-bin-Tughlaq).
**Music**: Indo-Persian synthesis — **qawwali, ghazal**; growth of **Hindustani** classical.
Qutb Minar (Aibak/Iltutmish) → Alai Darwaza (Khilji, first true dome) → Tughlaq batter-wall forts → Lodi tombs.
Amir Khusrau = qawwali, Khari Boli, Persian poetry — a favourite name.

prelimsPointers: **Qutb Minar** — begun by **Aibak**, completed by **Iltutmish**; **Quwwat-ul-Islam** — first mosque in India.
**Alai Darwaza** (Alauddin Khilji) — first building with a **true dome and true arch**.
**Tughlaq** architecture — austere, **sloping (batter) walls**; **Tughlaqabad fort**.
**Lodi Gardens** — octagonal tombs, early **double dome**.
**Amir Khusrau** — 'Parrot of India'; pioneered **qawwali, Khari Boli (Hindavi)**, credited with sitar/tabla legend.
Historians — **Ziauddin Barani (Tarikh-i-Firozshahi), Minhaj-us-Siraj (Tabaqat-i-Nasiri)**.
Style = **Indo-Islamic** (arch-dome-minaret + Indian decorative craft).
Sultanate = **arcuate** (arch-dome) style; **Alai Darwaza** = first **true dome** (Alauddin).
**Amir Khusrau** — father of **Qawwali**, Khari Boli/Urdu; Tuti-i-Hind; **Ibn Battuta** wrote **Rihla**.
**Ziauddin Barani** — Tarikh-i-Firozshahi; **Minhaj-us-Siraj** — Tabaqat-i-Nasiri.
**Qutb Minar** (Aibak/Iltutmish); Tughlaqabad; **Lodi double-dome** tombs.
mainsAngles: Discuss the evolution of Indo-Islamic architecture under the Delhi Sultanate.

glossary.definition: Construction using arches and domes (as against the Indian trabeate/beam style), introduced by the Sultanate.
Alauddin Khilji's gateway at the Qutb complex, India's first true dome and arch.
The Sultanate's greatest Persian poet-musician, credited with qawwali and the roots of Khari Boli/Urdu.

blocks.text: The **Vijayanagara Empire (1336–1646)** was the **great Hindu power of the south**, founded by **Harihara and Bukka (Sangama dynasty)** to resist the Sultanates. Peaking under **Krishnadevaraya (Tuluva dynasty)**, it fostered a **golden age of Telugu-Kannada-Sanskrit culture** and the **Hampi** architecture, until **Talikota (1565)**. Its rival was the **Bahmani Sultanate**.

rows: **Harihara & Bukka (Sangama)**; then **Saluva, Tuluva, Aravidu**; capital **Vijayanagara (Hampi)** on the Tungabhadra.
Greatest (Tuluva); **Amuktamalyada**; court of **Ashtadiggajas** (Peddana); defeated the Gajapatis & Bahmanis.
**Bahmani Sultanate (1347, Alauddin Hasan Bangda Shah, capital Gulbarga→Bidar)**; **Mahmud Gawan** (great PM); split into 5 **Deccan Sultanates**.
The **Deccan Sultanates' confederacy** defeated Vijayanagara — the empire declined.
Foreign travellers — **Nicolo Conti, Abdur Razzaq, Domingo Paes, Nuniz**.

items: **Founded 1336** by **Harihara & Bukka (Sangama)** (guided by **Vidyaranya**), capital **Hampi (Vijayanagara)** on the Tungabhadra — a Hindu bulwark against the **Bahmani** Sultanate.

**Four dynasties**: Sangama → Saluva → **Tuluva** (**Krishnadevaraya** — greatest, 1509–29; author of **Amuktamalyada** in Telugu & Sanskrit; the **Ashtadiggajas** poets incl. **Allasani Peddana** 'Andhrakavita Pitamaha'; defeated Gajapatis & Bahmanis) → Aravidu; **Battle of Talikota/Rakshasa-Tangadi (1565)** — the Deccan Sultanates crushed Vijayanagara (Rama Raya killed) & sacked Hampi.
**Administration**: the **Nayankara** (military-feudal governors) & **Ayagar** (village-servant) systems; heavy standing army & cavalry (imported horses via **Portuguese**); land revenue **1/6**.

**Economy & accounts**: prosperous — foreign travellers **Nicolo Conti, Abdur Razzaq** ('no city like it'), **Domingo Paes, Fernao Nuniz** (Portuguese) describe wealth, markets, temples; irrigation tanks; the **Vittala (musical pillars, stone chariot) & Virupaksha & Hazara Rama temples**, Lotus Mahal, elephant stables — Hampi = **UNESCO** site.
**Culture**: **raya gopurams**, temple towns; patronage of Telugu/Kannada/Tamil/Sanskrit; Carnatic music codification.
Four dynasties (Sangama-Saluva-Tuluva-Aravidu); Krishnadevaraya + Ashtadiggajas + Hampi; Talikota 1565.
Bahmani → Mahmud Gawan → split into 5 Deccan Sultanates → confederacy at Talikota.

prelimsPointers: Vijayanagara founded (1336) by **Harihara & Bukka (Sangama dynasty)**; capital **Hampi** on the **Tungabhadra**.
Four dynasties — **Sangama, Saluva, Tuluva, Aravidu**.
**Krishnadevaraya** (Tuluva) — greatest; wrote **Amuktamalyada**; court of the **Ashtadiggajas** (Allasani Peddana).
**Hampi** — UNESCO site; **Vitthala temple (stone chariot, musical pillars)** & **Virupaksha temple** are its masterpieces.
**Bahmani Sultanate (1347)** — founder **Alauddin Hasan (Bahman Shah)**; capital **Gulbarga → Bidar**; PM **Mahmud Gawan**.
Bahmani split into **five Deccan Sultanates** — Bijapur (Adil Shahi), Golconda (Qutb Shahi), Ahmadnagar (Nizam Shahi), Bidar (Barid Shahi), Berar (Imad Shahi).
**Battle of Talikota/Rakshasi-Tangadi (1565)** — Deccan confederacy defeated Vijayanagara.
Foreign visitors — **Abdur Razzaq (Persia), Nicolo Conti (Italy), Domingo Paes & Nuniz (Portugal)**.
Vijayanagara founded **1336** by **Harihara & Bukka**, capital **Hampi**; guru **Vidyaranya**.
**Krishnadevaraya** (Tuluva) — **Amuktamalyada**; **Ashtadiggajas** (Allasani Peddana); Telugu golden age.
**Battle of Talikota (1565)** — Deccan Sultanates destroyed Vijayanagara/Hampi.
Systems: **Nayankara** (feudal governors) & **Ayagar** (village servants); land tax ~1/6.
Travellers: **Abdur Razzaq, Nicolo Conti, Domingo Paes, Fernao Nuniz**; Hampi = **UNESCO** (Vittala/Virupaksha temples).
mainsAngles: Assess Vijayanagara as a bastion of south-Indian Hindu culture; and the causes of its decline at Talikota.

glossary.definition: The 'eight elephants' — eight Telugu poets of Krishnadevaraya's court, led by Allasani Peddana.
The 1565 battle where the Deccan Sultanates' confederacy defeated Vijayanagara.
The reforming prime minister of the Bahmani Sultanate at its height.
